clue.text: (& 2dn.) Latin gonads do when mangled (not one for risky chance)

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to leave out a single letter that the word 'one' stands for
something mangled is crushed out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for Latin
taken as written
taken as written
'a' means one; this letter is the one removed

explanation.surface: A mock-Latin anatomical joke about testicles getting mangled, with a coy aside about luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one A from L plus GONADS plus DO, then rearrange the rest to get LONG ODDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Long odds describe an outcome that is unlikely, so a bet on them is a risky chance.

clue.text: see 1dn.
Turn white when prolific scorer grabs left testicle's tip

indicators.note: to grab is to take hold of, so the scorer's name wraps around the other letters
a tip is an end point, here the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: J. S. Bach wrote musical scores in vast numbers
L is the abbreviation for left
the last letter of testicle

explanation.surface: A footballer who scores freely seizes an opponent below the belt and goes pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prolific scorer' suggests a striker, but it is a composer: a score is written music. B(LE)ACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach something is to make it, or let it become, white or pale.

clue.text: see 21ac.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' suggests inflating a doll; here it is an explosive. T(RIDE)NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannia, the female figure personifying Britain, is shown holding a three-pronged spear, a trident.

clue.text: Experimental holds to grip love in the sack – murder!

explanation.walkthrough: There are two containers here, one inside the other: love sits inside the rearranged letters, and that group sits inside the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshed is killing or violent slaughter, which the exclamation 'murder!' stands for here.

clue.text: Elected, on the up, taken to party's heart – then shut out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a political party, but here it is a celebration. BA(NI)SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to exclude or expel them, which is what shutting them out means.

clue.text: Freak Miliband rejected by electoral action (ultimately Conservative)

the final letter of Conservative

explanation.walkthrough: Freak here is the noun meaning an enthusiast, as in 'fitness freak', not an oddity.

clue.text: Protest/action group having got the chop?

explanation.walkthrough: Hacked Off is the UK campaign for a free and accountable press, founded after the phone-hacking scandal; the phrase also means chopped off, and in slang annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The campaign's name is the phrase itself, and something that got the chop has literally been severed by hacking.

clue.text: After brief "no", First Lady gets end away, which is very dry

clue.text: Liberal, familiar ex-tabloid female editor's listed for bad behaviour – unlikely to improve tabloid standards?
